claim: Special-value handling precedes positive finite digit generation; local arithmetic and caller buffers perform the work. Formatting returns a length, does not terminate or check cap, and allocates no shared state. Callers provide the stated fixed buffers.

The constructor copies into its 256-byte array or owned string, then stores a pointer into that storage. No copy rebasing, allocation catch or publication is implemented; parsers use stack instances and borrow get().

Slice stores a borrowed pointer/length/namespace. Key equality adds identity; value equality ignores namespace. SmallBuf owns inline/malloc storage and frees growth, but plain size changes provide no publication. Growth has no malloc-failure/overflow handling; direct commits and input lifetimes require caller discipline. Conn and WbEngine both commit bytes.

Boot preparation and fixtures populate plain vectors. Declaration checks affinity, duplicates and syntax but can leave partial state; discovery has per-CPU fallback and sibling discovery requires sysfs. Queries require serialized mutation and valid cpus_in indices; vector exceptions are uncaught.

Preparation allocates the trailing slots/key tail; installation bounds count by capacity. FlatStore links and retires records and balances retained group state, including shutdown. Group decisions use acquire loads; plain lists do not publish across threads.

PINs own copied keys; unit-intent allocations prefix UnitRef while kind-0 pins do not. Plain refs/links require owner serialization; activity transitions use release RMWs. Allocation failure is reported by pin helpers. Command code retains decision targets, and group-unit destruction releases watch_refs.

The store owns lazy state, intrusive pools and plain counters. Extension initializes the discriminator before arming; combined finish-install touches only the installing/group-count bytes. FreeValue overlays dead value storage. Allocator failures belong to the prepare helpers; shutdown releases state.

Both decision and owner paths update relaxed atomic counters and INFO samples them. The inline global is separately compiled per namespace and cannot provide a coherent multi-field publication snapshot.

Resolver results and collapse/seen-key scratch borrow objects, records and key bytes; the owning traversal transfers/retires them. Scratch indices use index+1 with zero empty; these aggregates have no independent lifetime or publication operation.

execute_flush installs on the owner and handles null as OOM before linking. Poison precedes range linkage; release unlinks, recounts saturated ranges, closes poison and release-decrements refs/activity. Invalid release input aborts; shutdown also releases ranges after joining.

Local vectors own scratch; slots borrow stable key storage and parked-slot addresses. Sixteen hash probes fall back to increasing-bit Patricia descent, using 64 hash bits, eight namespace bits and nine per key byte. First insertion wins; allocation exceptions are caught before mutation by atomic_flush_erase.

The owner admits a ready range after snapshot preservation. Scratch capacity/allocation refusal returns false before changing residents; execute_flush defers it. Erasure releases tombstones before deferred retirement, clears first-post predecessor slots, and preserves unarmed send-borrow retirement. The deferred queue supplies writer back-pressure.

Owner-local resolution returns borrowed physical/parked state with acquire group decisions. Same-connection floors precede visibility filtering and own epoch-zero values rank first. There is no allocation or ordinary wait; the armed diagnostic alone re-polls at most 4096 times and does not replace the selected answer.

The shard owner publishes before mutation and closes after safety; readers acquire cell/epoch words. Cells are release-stored before release epochs. Saturation stays positive until exact drain; total/nesting overflow poisons permanently and detected underflows abort. uint32_t epoch increment can wrap; no suspension bound is established.

Per-physical-owner plain lists reuse post-grace blocks; migration changes future sink/cache access. put rejection retains caller ownership; take transfers a block or misses. Capacity checks and detected corruption are explicit, with a relaxed INFO byte gauge. Shutdown after joins also drains; the aggregate itself has no destructor cleanup.

Flag accesses are atomic but compound operators are load/store pairs, not RMWs. Foreign eviction CAS is unretried and approximate; immutable published string layout/content depends on caller replacement/QSBR. Header/tail accessors borrow storage and assume correct encoding/capacity; OwnsExtern selects destruction.

The object tail owns metadata and subsequent packed bytes; memcpy handles unaligned fields. No destructor/allocation/publication/bounds checks exist in the overlay. Constructor/adopt helpers populate aux fields for hash, set or stream and leave list/zset aux values zero.

Views/iterators borrow embedded or external storage, without publication/lifetime retention. Default views require binding and current positions. Embedded mutations validate boundaries/capacity and do not allocate; external ones delegate. CollectionRef guards compact mutation by encoding, but compact/aux access has representation preconditions. Inputs must survive mutation.

The scratch parameter is unused by string_value, which borrows object bytes. Raw initialization fills caller memory, rejects null/over-threshold inputs and allocates nothing. Factory and cached-block callers establish storage size and later publication; key/value sources must not overlap writes.

Install release-publishes fixed links and accounts nodes incrementally; false retains partial nodes. cell acquires links; timestamps use relaxed operations and one strong CAS attempt. Store configuration publishes/retires clocks; reclamation or quiescent teardown permits recursive node destruction. Missing cells/timestamps fall back.

The sink borrows queue/cache/context until callbacks finish, forwards without validation, and the real queue can wait for ring space. seq_cst epoch RMW plus grace floor is outside these helpers. Resize records are preallocated, transfer table ownership to a FIFO and free it on pop; stamps must be ordered, and unconditional drains/destruction need quiescence.

Vectors own encoded storage and the optional circular index; entry/iterator views borrow it. Index allocation starts above 16 entries. Growth may relocate before a later failure; spans and source lifetimes are caller preconditions. Guarded allocation/bounds failures return false, while generated vector copying can throw. No synchronization is implemented.

The base owns Compact and counters; derived structures own expanded data. Promotion records totals before clearing Compact, requiring prior copies in the destination. Guarded methods refuse expanded values; no demotion method, publication or wait exists here.

Hash destruction deletes field map and TTL side state; hash helpers maintain separate logical/TTL totals. Each ListNode owns Compact and borrows chain links; ListVal deletes its chain. Handlers build/attach nodes and serialize resident mutations; wrappers supply no publication.

Deque nodes own their packed logs, whose first entry carries the header. StreamVal owns nodes, indices/dictionaries and opaque groups; its destructor releases groups. Stream handlers construct/mutate and maintain totals; borrowed node storage requires caller lifetime protection.

Set slots own strings; the table owns slots and dense indices. Rebuild changes generation, erase leaves tombs, and borrowed values can expire. Insert/reserve distinguish checked refusal/OOM. Set promotion uses logical integer payload totals; ZsetVal deletes its expanded pointer. Resident mutation is caller-serialized with no wrapper publication.
